writeup: TIC 434321668 is a candidate eclipsing binary star with an orbital period of 11.127701 days and a primary eclipse depth of 18.48 percent. The binary was detected in automated TESS photometry analysis using the Box Least Squares algorithm, which achieved a signal-to-noise ratio of 151.6. Pixel-level difference imaging confirmed the signal with a peak signal-to-noise of 10.0, though the centroid offset of 3.1 arcseconds from the target warrants further investigation. The secondary eclipse was not detected. One notable caveat: alternating eclipses show significantly different depths, suggesting the true orbital period may be double the initially measured value. The object does not appear in six major variable-star catalogs, making it a previously uncatalogued candidate.
